SummaryCroc's back, and this time he's searching for his long-lost parents. Revived by the Dantinis, arch enemy Baron Dante vows revenge. Explore four mainland villages, rescue Gobbos, and battle new Guardians. Race cars and speedboats, ride minecarts, and take to the skies in the remastered 1999 classic.

Nov 3, 2026

Gaming Age
Croc 2 Kingdom of the Gobbos is one of those “if it ain’t broke, don’t fix it” remakes that fix only what needed improvement from the original game, leaving everything else intact. The gameplay, fun factor and overall presentation is exactly that of the original with a fresh coat of paint. There needs to be more remakes like this. Big Boat and Titanium did a wonderful job here. While I wasn’t fan of Croc back in the day, I’ve certainly become one now. Give this one a try, it doesn’t disappoint.

Oct 29, 2026
75
Noisy Pixel
Croc 2: Kingdom of the Gobbos is an enjoyable but uneven sequel that expands on the original with larger worlds, more varied gameplay, and added exploration. Not every new idea improves the experience, particularly its consumable upgrade system and inconsistent side activities, but charming characters, solid platforming, modernized controls, and an exceptional collection of archival bonus content make this remaster a worthwhile revival.
PlayStation 5 FULL REVIEW
Oct 29, 2026
70
Spilstrøm
The gameplay in Croc 2: Kingdom of the Gobbos has not aged particularly well, and in 2026, it feels like an exceedingly simple 3D platformer. It is a decent game to play with younger children who want to dip their toes into the world of 3D platformers, but others may find it a little too simplistic. There is no denying, however, that this is a thoroughly accomplished remaster, featuring plenty of visual options and a wealth of fascinating bonus content that will be a real treat for fans of the adorable little crocodile.
PlayStation 5 FULL REVIEW

GamersRD
While Croc 2: Kingdom of the Gobbos is an easy recommendation for nostalgic players and platforming enthusiasts, it remains very much a product of its time that still holds onto its charm. Its additions don't revolutionize the genre and things can feel a bit repetitive, but it stands as an accessible, lighthearted pick for younger gamers.

Oct 29, 2026
60
TheGamer
Croc might not be the first name that springs to mind when you think of colorful ‘90s platforming mascots, but the little green guy is very much a part of the conversation. I’m glad that, in an era when game preservation is increasingly prioritized, Croc hasn’t been forgotten. What’s more, if you ever want there to be a new Croc game, finally, after all these years, then these remasters need to sell well to show Argonaut that we Croc fans are still out there, waiting for the trilogy to finally be finished.
PlayStation 5
Oct 29, 2026
55
Gamesurf
Croc 2 Remastered is a difficult project to understand. It’s hard to tell whether this is pure nostalgia bait or an attempt to test the waters for a franchise reboot, but either way, it falls short of its goal. It’s tough to score positively: the new graphic modes and minor control tweaks represent the absolute bare minimum for a remaster, amounting to little more than a superficial coat of paint that fails to bring the game up to modern platforming standards. We may be living in an era of classic game revivals, but that doesn't mean every title from the past automatically deserves to be exhumed.
PlayStation 5 FULL REVIEW
